- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often overfits recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a spike (e.g., 10–15% drop in 3 days), model often fails to anticipate; add 1–3% downward bias for next 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to overfit short-term swings; dampen forecast volatility by 10–15%.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is rising sharply, model underestimates momentum; increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day.
